text: Just behind me is the Chinuan People's Hospital where most of the people who survived the
attack are recovering. 128 people are said to have been hospitalized directly after that blast.
First of all, we know from authorities that there are still toxic gases present in the mine,
so it's very difficult for rescue operators to get deep inside there. They're still waiting
or finding a way to dispel those gases. We don't know exactly what those fumes are,
but we do know that this is a high methane facility. We also know that the depth and
steep gradient of the shaft leading down to the mine is very difficult. It's making it
very difficult for rescue workers to get in there and to explore. Also, we know that there's rising
water in the areas underneath the ground that are affected, so they're also worried that there's
some sort of burst water pipes also complicating this rescue operation. And lastly, we have found
out that the blueprints that the authorities were given after this blast occurred were actually not
accurate. They do not match the layout underground in the mine, so that's forcing
rescue workers to have to improvise in their operations, and so it's taking more time than
they expected to recover all of those miners who were underneath when this took place.
